title: test(vi-mock): inherit the real @object-ui/components surface in 27 vi.mock factories
body:
Part of #6892 — slice 6 of the per-specifier `vi.mock` sweep worklist: `@object-ui/components`.

All 27 frozen `@object-ui/components` factories now obtain the real module through `importOriginal` and SPREAD it first, and the specifier joins `COVERED_SPECIFIERS` in `scripts/check-vi-mock-inherit.mjs` in the same change — the gate's documented widening precondition, never a judgement.

Base (merge-base) `336a9eb8a`. Head `214d5d5a6`, after merging `origin/main` mid-slice. Every figure below is pinned to that head unless it says otherwise.

## STEP 0 — the barrel walk, and why the slice proceeded

`packages/components/src` is the largest barrel this worklist has met: **205 modules and 1173 module-scope statements** reached from `index.ts`. It is NOT inert, and it was never expected to be — objectui#7837 had already counted the registrations. What decided the slice is the CLASS of the effect, measured three independent ways.

**Statically.** 112 module-scope `ComponentRegistry.register(...)` call sites, and **every one of them passes a namespace** (`ui` 85, `element` 10, `page` 7, `action` 5, plus the loop-driven `protocol-placeholder` marks; the five in `layout/page.tsx` that look bare carry `namespace: 'ui'` through the spread `pageMeta`). `register()` itself was READ, not assumed — `packages/core/src/registry/Registry.ts:433` is a `Map.set` into an in-memory registry, a `console.warn` on the un-namespaced spelling that therefore cannot fire, a bare-name collision guard, and a `notify()` over a listener `Set` that is empty at import time. Beyond registration there is **exactly one** non-allocation statement in the whole graph: `hooks/related-count-store.ts` calls `subscribeDataChanges`, which `packages/react/src/data-invalidation.ts` implements as a `Set.add` into a module-level listener set — no timer, no window listener, no request.

**By grep, column-anchored, over all 205 reached modules.** The timers / globals / storage / network / DOM pattern matches nothing (grep exit 1). The IDENT-dot-method pattern (`register` / `init` / `configure` / `addEventListener` / `subscribe` / `on` / `start` / `connect` / `listen`) returns the `ComponentRegistry.register` lines and nothing else.

**Empirically.** Importing the real barrel in the happy-dom environment moves the registry from 0 to **295 keys over 159 `register()` calls**, exports 351 names, and emits **ZERO `console.warn` and ZERO `console.error`**. (159 exceeds the 112 static sites because three module-scope loops register per element — the seven semantic tags, the raw HTML tags, and the four palette placeholder blocks.)

**The consuming side**, which is the failure class the ruling names. Of the 27 converted files, **none names `ComponentRegistry` at all** — so nothing asserts registry emptiness, a registration count, or a `get()` of a key the barrel now claims. Six `console.warn` spies exist across four of them; all six are installed inside `it(...)` bodies (after import, so a collection-time registration is invisible to them) AND filter their calls by message content. No assertion in the swept set can observe a registration.

**The CSS question (A3).** The barrel has exactly one side-effect import and it is CSS — `./sidebar-fixes.css`, plain CSS by construction; the barrel's own comment explains at length why the Tailwind entry is deliberately NOT imported there. The root Vitest config declares no `css` option, so CSS is not processed and the import is inert under happy-dom. That is corroborated rather than argued: **20 sites on this specifier already inherited the real barrel on `main`** and passed, 8 of them in `packages/app-shell` under the LIGHT `dom` project. That is the free confirmation slice 4 did not have.

**Verdict: PROCEED**, on the benign class slices 2 and 5 absorbed.

## STEP 1 — the census, re-derived, never inherited

Derived through the gate's exported `scan()` with `covered` set to all 22 workspace specifiers any `vi.mock` call site in the tree names. `COVERED_SPECIFIERS` was **never** widened-and-reverted in the tree.

| | judged | inheriting | frozen |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@object-ui/components` before | 47 | 20 | **27** |
| `@object-ui/components` after | 47 | 47 | **0** |

All-specifier population over the same 22 specifiers: **150 frozen before, 123 after, over 659 judged**, 0 unreadable. A diff of the two per-specifier tables with the components row removed is **empty** — every other one of the 21 rows byte-identical, zero sites moved the other way. Identical on the merged head.

The gate's own verdict line at `214d5d5a6`:

```
check-vi-mock-inherit: OK (4384 tracked source file(s), 2659 test-named; 603 carry a mock;
486 call site(s) on ... @object-ui/components judged (486 inherit, 0 auto-mocked);
173 other workspace, 236 external, 873 local, 0 non-static, 3 embedded in a string literal)
```

486 judged over eleven covered specifiers, up from 439 over ten.

The dispatch's grep upper bound was exact in total (47 files naming the specifier) and the frozen subset distributes **24 `packages/app-shell` / 2 `packages/plugin-detail` / 1 `packages/plugin-timeline`** — the remaining 20 were the already-inheriting sites, 12 of them in `packages/plugin-form`.

## The three syntactic shapes

1. **Object-literal arrow** — 16 sites. The factory becomes `async (importOriginal)` and the awaited spread is the first property.
2. **Block-bodied arrow with a `return`** — 6 sites. The factory awaits into `actual` on its first line and the returned object spreads it first, so hand-written helpers defined in the body still close over what they need.
3. **Already `async`, and still frozen** — 5 sites. These awaited something OTHER than the module under mock (React, or one deep-relative source module) and returned a hand-listed object. This is precisely the shape a name-matching gate waves through and the semantic recogniser does not; all five now await `importOriginal` as well.

In every shape the real module is spread FIRST and the hand-written overrides come after, so every stub the suite depends on still wins and every other export is the real one.

## ⭐ What inheriting actually broke, and where it was repaired

This is the first slice where converted files **died during COLLECTION**, which is the failure this whole worklist describes, observed from the other side. 15 of the 27 died at once, on one cause:

```
Caused by: Error: [vitest] No "Info" export is defined on the "lucide-react" mock.
  packages/components/src/notifications/severity.ts:46:11
  packages/components/src/notifications/NotificationBanners.tsx:28:1
```

The real barrel reaches `notifications/severity.ts`, which reads four icons from `lucide-react` **at module scope** into a `const` table — and those 15 files carried their own frozen `lucide-react` factory that had never listed them. Product source was not touched: the repair is the **neighbouring factory**, converted to the same inheriting form (spread the real module first, keep every hand-written icon stub after it). A frozen THIRD-PARTY factory can therefore be the thing that blocks a workspace-specifier sweep, even though this gate never judges one — worth carrying into the remaining slices.

One follow-up commit removes something the freeze had forced: both `DeclaredActionsBar` suites reached `hasDeclaredVisibilityGate` through a deep relative path into `packages/components/src`, with a paragraph explaining that the barrel "stays doubled". With the barrel inherited the real re-export arrives on its own, so the path and the paragraph are both gone; the suites stay green at 50 tests, which is what shows it is the same function.

## Residuals

**Zero.** No site was left frozen and none was excluded. The one file that documented itself as deliberately doubling the barrel was `DeclaredActionsBar.test.tsx` — its stated reason was the light `dom` project's setup cost, not a semantic claim about the barrel not being loaded, and 8 app-shell files in that same project already inherit the barrel today. It was converted, and its prose rewritten rather than left describing a tree that no longer exists.

## Cost — measured, not absorbed silently (A2)

The `dom` / `dom-heavy` project split exists precisely to keep this package's graph out of the light project's setup, so a converted file now pulls it through its own imports instead. Per file, twice each, on one app-shell suite:

| | run 1 | run 2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| frozen | 6.17s | 5.97s |
| inheriting the barrel and `lucide-react` | 8.72s | 9.36s |

At the WHOLE-PACKAGE level it does not aggregate, because the module graph is shared within a worker across a run: `packages/app-shell` on four disjoint shards totals **792s over 635 files** here, against the **961s over 634 files** slice 5 measured on the same suite by the same method. So the honest reading is "a converted file costs about half again as much cold, and the package suite does not move" — recorded rather than accepted in silence.

## Tests

- **The 27 converted files**: exit 0, **27 files / 265 tests**. The SAME 27 paths with their merge-base blobs restored: exit 0, **27 files / 265 tests** — no test lost or gained, nothing died during collection. The restore was proven on disk (the awaited-spread marker across the 27 paths goes 154 to 70, and 22 frozen non-async heads reappear) and left `git diff HEAD` naming zero paths.
- **`packages/app-shell`**: exit 0 on **four disjoint shards whose union is the package** — 159 + 159 + 159 + 158 = 635 files, 1570 + 1326 + 1706 + 1506 = 6108 passed plus 1 skipped. A single invocation exceeds this container's foreground cap; each shard ran in the foreground to completion.
- **`packages/plugin-detail` + `packages/plugin-timeline`**: exit 0, 158 files / 1508 tests, one invocation.
- **The gate's own test family** (its pin, plus the two other suites that name the script): exit 0, 3 files / 176 tests. The pin is **67 of 67** and was NOT edited — the header record was worded around objectui#8117 (no backtick-quoted test-file name followed by a comma or a bracket), and a local re-run of that assertion's own regex over the edited gate source returns zero matches.

**Ablation — three legs, ONE PER SHAPE**, each taken from the committed tree, each mutation proven on disk by anchored marker counts BEFORE the result is read, each restore proven by `git hash-object` equalling the HEAD blob AND by `git diff HEAD` naming zero paths — never by a checkout exit code:

| shape | file | mutation | gate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 object-literal | `packages/plugin-timeline/src/ObjectTimeline.test.tsx` | drop the awaited spread (2 markers to 0) | exit 1, names line 42 for this specifier (and line 8 for `@object-ui/react`, whose factory shares the marker — the leg removes both) |
| 2 block-bodied | `packages/app-shell/src/hooks/__tests__/sharedInboxFeed.twoSurfaces.test.tsx` | drop `...actual` from the returned object (1 to 0) | exit 1, names line 95, one factory |
| 3 already-async | `packages/app-shell/src/layout/__tests__/ContextSelectors.scopeKey.test.tsx` | drop `...actual` from the returned object (1 to 0) | exit 1, names line 36, one factory |

Legs 2 and 3 exercise the gate's "obtaining without SPREADING is still frozen" rule specifically: `importOriginal` is still called on the line above. Restored, the gate reads exit 0 each time. No dist preflight is needed — the root Vitest config aliases the specifier to `packages/components/src` and the gate is a source-text scanner.

`Live E2E (informational)` is red on every branch today for an upstream reason (objectui#7990 / objectstack#16186), not this change.

## Out of scope, filed not fixed

objectui#8141 — the gate's covered set is exact-match, so a SUBPATH of an already-swept package is counted and never judged. Measured at this head: 2 such call sites exist (`@object-ui/components/ui/sonner`), both already inheriting, so tightening it is free today. Not touched here: changing what the scope resolver accepts is a different decision from sweeping one specifier.
